label: Deepened Nishida’s Logic of Basho into an existential-ontological philosophy of Sunyata
description: As Nishida’s foremost Kyoto School successor, Nishitani shifted the axis from pure experience and basho to the existential passage through nihility into Emptiness (ku/sunyata).
dialecticalTension: Systematizes Kyoto School philosophy as an explicit answer to European nihilism.

label: Studied under Heidegger in Freiburg, then critiqued Western ontology for halting at nihility
description: Nishitani engaged Heidegger’s Being and Time directly in 1937–1939, arguing that Heidegger’s "nothingness" remained tethered to a standpoint of finitude rather than sunyata’s self-emptying.
dialecticalTension: Stages the premier 20th-century dialogue between Continental phenomenology and Zen ontology.

label: Synthesized Nietzsche’s active nihilism with Mahayana emptiness to overcome ego-centered will
description: Nishitani credited Nietzsche with diagnosing European nihilism, yet argued that the Will to Power remains trapped in self-assertion unless emptied into non-substantial sunyata.
dialecticalTension: Transforms Nietzschean self-overcoming into Buddhist non-ego realization.

label: Reframed Basho as the field of Sunyata where every entity interpenetrates without substance
description: In Religion and Nothingness, Nishitani articulated the field of emptiness (sunyata) as the circuminsessional ground unifying Nishida’s basho with Huayan interpenetration.
dialecticalTension: Connects Kyoto School spatial logic to classical Mahayana emptiness.
